title: WorkCharter
description: Declares the intent and direction of a unit of work (a sprint and/or a branch) BEFORE the work starts. Lives at .council/charters/sprint-NN.json (council-owned working file; mutable, NOT append-only). Consumed by scripts/direction-check.py (Layer A deterministic tripwires) and the direction-guardian agent (Layer B semantic judge). The exploration_mode field is the single 'flag' that propagates to the git hook (Surface 2) and the GitHub PR/Action (Surface 3): divergent work is legitimate WHEN declared, flagged when silent. See instructions/direction-check.md.

sprint_context.description: The sprint number this charter governs, when the work is harness-sprint-scoped.

branch.description: The git branch this work lands on. Used by the branch-charter git hook (Surface 2) to decide whether a divergent branch has a declared purpose.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the charter was authored.

created_by.description: Human or agent id that authored the charter.

strategic_anchor.description: The strategic-anchor document this work must stay aligned with (e.g. a divorce-spec). Drift from the anchor is the failure this whole mechanism exists to catch.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the strategic-anchor doc, e.g. docs/divorce-spec.md.

cited_section.description: The specific section / rule of the anchor this work is reconciled against.

locked_decisions.description: Identifiers of binding decisions the work must honor, e.g. ['ADR-0008'].

workstream_scope.description: The workstream names this work touches. Each should map to a workstream the anchor recognizes (or be declared as a divergence).

exploration_mode.description: mainline = work on the sanctioned direction; any anchor drift here is undeclared and BLOCKS. parallel-exploration = a deliberate side-track that may diverge (e.g. a spike). competitive = an intentional competing implementation tested against mainline ('competitive code development'). For the two non-mainline modes, divergence is legitimate but MUST carry a divergence_justification.

anchor_alignment.description: Per-workstream assertion that the work aligns with the anchor (or is a declared divergence). Optional but recommended; the Layer B judge reads it.

divergence_justification.description: REQUIRED when exploration_mode is parallel-exploration or competitive (enforced by direction-check.py, not by this schema alone, so a mainline charter need not carry it). Records WHY the work diverges from the anchor and the competing hypothesis being tested.

direction_check.description: Last verdict written back by direction-check.py / direction-guardian. Lets the trine-eval seam read a pre-computed verdict without executing any council code.

findings.description: Human-readable list of the checks that fired.
